doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Leaving JATP over its circus atmosphere
summary: After about four and a half years, Jones left JATP because showmanship overtook the music.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And you continued to tour with that band until when? I have here until 1961.
In to 1951. I started in 1947… Perhaps the end of 1950. It was about four years. I guess it was about four and half years.
Was it artistically satisfying? I know you said that you got a chance to play with a lot of people. I don't want to say that it was hokey, but there seem to be a show business piece of it.

That is the part of it that really turned me off, to use an old time Warner expression. You see, when I joined it, I joined it because I thought it would be a great musical experience, not a circus. When it took on a certain circus complex, I lost interest in. I said that it was time for me to leave. They started playing to the people in the top of the office they were the screeners. If you did something that was visual,

not something you get here… A lot of the things that guys played on the stage were great musically. But, they didn't have the same reaction as when some guy was screaming, or laying a high note on the horn. He was down on the stage flopping like a fish out of water. Is kind of things turned me off. I said, "This is not music. This is not what I joined it for. I'm going to leave.”
